note: web.archive.org was unreachable from this coder's fetch tool; all verification used dated pre-election news articles fetched directly (dates are article publication dates). Post-election sidebar content was ignored.

GOV-MI.name: Jocelyn Benson
GOV-MI.evidence: Two-term Secretary of State running as continuity of Whitmer record; slogan 'Costs down, wages up and end corruption'; conventional party-line platform (drug affordability board, school funding); no left or centrist markers.

GOV-VT.name: Amanda Janoo
GOV-VT.evidence: First-time candidate/economist cast as 'progressive political outsider' who beat establishment-cast Aly Richards; ran on economic inequality, taxes on wealthy and big tech, universal primary care; Sanders endorsed, 'movement for economic justice'.

SEN-MN.name: Peggy Flanagan
SEN-MN.evidence: Ran as the progressive vs Jeffries/Pelosi/Buttigieg-backed Angie Craig; Medicare for all, 'ripping apart' ICE, 'radical change'; endorsed by Sanders and Warren. Sitting Lt. Gov. with institutional support (Sen. Tina Smith), so mixed rather than populist.

PA-11.name: Nancy Mannion
PA-11.evidence: Emergency nurse/healthcare consultant; conventional priorities (affordable healthcare, education, voting rights); NOW endorsement; 'powered by people - not billionaires' tagline only; no left or centrist markers.

CO-4.name: Eileen Laubacher
CO-4.evidence: Retired Navy rear admiral, registered Democrat only in 2025; bipartisan framing ('we agree on far more than our politics suggests', 'people ahead of politics'); border security plus reform; term/age limits and stock-trading ban add some anti-Washington tone.

TX-25.name: Dione Sims
TX-25.evidence: Community organizer/nonprofit founder (Opal Lee's granddaughter); priorities living/prevailing wage, affordable healthcare, civil rights; endorsed by local Democratic officials (e.g. state Sen. Royce West); no left or centrist markers.

NJ-1.name: Donald Norcross
NJ-1.evidence: Six-term safe-seat incumbent; former IBEW electrician and South Jersey AFL-CIO president; conventional labor-Democrat platform. Labour background noted but campaign is institutional incumbent framing. Caucus membership not confirmed in fetched source.

SEN-LA.name: Jamie Davis
SEN-LA.evidence: Third-generation farmer/'country boy' grassroots run; says he won't 'play into party politics', common ground with Republican farmers, pro-2A, border security, opposes taxpayer-funded youth gender surgery; but pro-choice, minimum wage hike, eventual Medicare-for-all option (mixed ideological signals).

OH-7.name: Brian Poindexter
OH-7.evidence: Union ironworker, 'that union guy that Democrats have lost'; economics over culture war, Sherrod Brown-style workers' rights; 'Politicians are completely out of touch'; Kucinich endorsement; no explicit centrist or left branding.

SEN-KS.name: Adam Hamilton
SEN-KS.evidence: Self-described 'independent minded Democrat' 'leading from the center'; considered running as independent; 'building bridges across the political aisle'; megachurch pastor and political newcomer.

MI-3.name: Hillary Scholten
MI-3.evidence: Swing-seat incumbent; Problem Solvers Caucus and New Democrat Coalition member (per secondary profiles, not confirmed in fetched dated source); 'People in this district vote for me, even if they don't agree with everything'.

GOV-WI.name: David Crowley
GOV-WI.evidence: Presented himself as a 'bridge builder,' a moderate Democrat who could work across the aisle; beat democratic socialist Francesca Hong; Evers endorsement; earlier withdrew to consolidate moderate voters.

FL-15.name: Robert People
FL-15.evidence: Army combat veteran; campaign site lists Medicare for All, corporate accountability, opposes AIPAC and arms to Israel (Track AIPAC endorsement); anti-oligarchy framing; no Sanders/OR/WFP/JD backing found, so not coded left.
